consensus_summary: The Lamb primarily and overwhelmingly denotes Jesus Christ as the unblemished sacrificial/atoning offering (Passover and related OT backgrounds) whose death redeems from sin, fused with the slain-yet-victorious, reigning Lamb of Revelation.
book_summary: Jesus Christ as the unblemished Passover sacrifice, slain to redeem His people and now reigning.
consensus_core_identification: Jesus Christ = the sacrificial redemptive Lamb (unblemished/Passover/atoning) who is also victorious and enthroned.
book_core_identification: Jesus Christ = the unblemished Passover sacrifice slain to redeem, now reigning.
boundary_disagreement: None; book’s concise wording stays inside the consensus core and does not add, drop, or reclassify cases relative to the shared christological-sacrificial-plus-reigning identification.
rationale: All four consensus responses converge on the identical central referent and dual aspect (sacrificial redemption + reigning victory) that the book states in abbreviated form. Differences are only length, emphasis among OT backgrounds, or listing of secondary non-titular uses of ‘lamb’; none alter the core identity. Extension is coextensive for the titular ‘Lamb’.
strongest_objection: None material; at most that the book omits explicit mention of secondary flock or counterfeit-lamb uses that consensus already treats as distinct from the primary title.
